## Rules

- The standing rules R1–R14: [13 §1](13-game-design.md#design-pillars). Most cited here: R1 (holo labels, four
  tiers), R8 (every motion means something), R9 (the drawn count is the true count), R10 (identity by more

  itself), R14 (attention is budgeted).
- The invariants: [02 §1](02-domain-rules.md#1-invariants), especially INV-12 and INV-15 (playing to *x* and
  seeking to *x* draw the same thing), INV-14 (stable slots), INV-18 (fixture data only) and INV-19 (no
  individual scoring).
- Story time's B-15 (05 §8.3a): order within a piece is never broken.
- Values go to [15](15-reference.md) in the same change. Departures from 02 and 03 are amended there and
  called out.
- Project lenses for the sluice's agents: `.claude/sluice/project.md`.

## Order and blocks

| Block | Items | Why this order | Human gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | A1, A2, A3, A4 | Quick carried fixes. A3's vsync budget is the yardstick B1 is measured against | Final check |
| B | B1, B2, B3, B4 | The carried looks. B1 (resting plates) goes first: it changes every scene's labels, which D and E lay out against | Final check |
| C | C1, C2, C4, C3 | Measure before cutting (decided): the pacing ledger, then each candidate's estimated saving; C4 makes budgets and switches a device profile; C3 (split from B1) cuts Pulsar's frame cost as profile switches | **HG-C, mid-tranche:** the user sets a target per pod size and picks which E items get built, and how far |
| D | D1, D2, D3 | Formation layout before the director (decided): it fixes crowding today and de-risks E6's larger union formations | Final check |
| E | E1–E10 | The pacing build, limited to what HG-C picked. E1 and E2 settle what's shown and counted; E3 and E4 give the director its forms; E5 decides between them; E6–E9 build on it | Final check |
| F | F1–F5 | Chains (asked 2026-11-06, picked by the user, so not gated by HG-C): a captain's run of summons or merges plays as one smooth maneuver. Built on E6's volleys and fuse (B-21), E7's sweep pattern (M-32), E4a's transform from the gather and D's formation spots. F1's fixture first, so every later item has a case; F2 changes every summon, F3 chains them, F4 chains merges; F5 (added 2026-11-06) fixes Meteor's hit floor at the small window. After E9 and block E's audit (F-Q4); its own block audit | Final check (with D and E), with a live walk of F1's run |

**Final check:** the D, E and F stills and live walks (A and B were signed 2026-11-01), with a live walk of F1's run and Comet's feel; the Azure CLI live check (v1.3's E5, waived to here;

**Sizing (a hint for the planner):** A1 is small (a clerk). A2–A4, B2–B4, C2 and D1 are medium. B1, C1, D2, D3
and E1–E9 are medium or large, by the planner's risk score: they touch the schedule, the interpreter or the
layout, which feed the goldens and the agreement between seek and play.

### F1 A bulk-PR run in the fixtures
- Asked:       The user saw, in a live session, one captain open a long run of automated PRs (36), each into its
               own repo, so each summons its own station, and later merge them all. No fixture has this. Fixture
               data only (INV-18): the run is rebuilt with invented names, never copied.
- Today:       The Halcyon pods (`fixtures/scenarios/halcyon/`) have no automation-style runs. Nothing has more
               than a few summons or merges by one captain in a row, and every E6 volley groups merges into one
               station. No fixture has an opening run either (E7b's tests are synthetic).
- Decided:     A new Halcyon pod (the planner picks an invented name), so the existing pods' goldens don't move,
               added to the pacing ledger's pods (C1). One captain opens 36 PRs into 36 repos within one minute,
               then merges them over that day and the next working day, with 3–5 approvers whose sets overlap and
               widen across the run. It also has the cases that bound a chain: the same captain's single summon;
               two merges more than a working day apart; another captain's beat between two links; a link the
               B-15 guard must refuse (its work touched between links); and a station where a second author's merge
               would also make an E6 volley (F-Q5).
- Acceptance:
  - `npm run fixtures` writes the pod. Its halcyon golden is added, and the other pods' goldens are unchanged.
  - The pod opens in `npm run dev` with 36 stations on its rings, with no layout overlap (VC-3 case).
  - The ledger has the pod's row, measured before F2.
- Risk:        fixture (small to medium).
- Touches:     `fixtures/scenarios/halcyon/{pods,runs,cast}.ts`, the halcyon goldens, `scripts/pacing-ledger.ts`.
- Depends on:  —
- State:       accepted; docs/progress/v1.4/work/F1/ (Meteor Pod, area 8005: 37 stations, the run's 36 plus the lone summon's; its own golden `halcyon-meteor.*`; the ledger takes it opt-in (`PodSpec.extra`), so no E row moves; VC-3 passes at 1440×900, and 1024×640 is `test.fail`, F5; amends 03's sprint-pods row)

### F2 Summon on the fly
- Asked:       "A captain will move to the station position, emit the call when reaching the station arrival point,
               but then keep moving without stopping. In the basic case of a captain setting up on a single PR, it
               saves the stop and go nature of it (while still correlating the objects because the captain's call
               blip should match the arrival effect of the station)."
- Today:       Station jump-in (`facility.enter`, 2.8 s: tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600; E1 retired the
               beacon pulses) flies the summoner to a spot beside the station, holds it there through the arrival
               and a second named (`crewHoldMs`, 22 B9), then flies it back over 0.8 s (`stationJumpIn.ts`).
               Summons aren't director moments (not protected), so no lever shortens them, and they aren't in
               the crowd's `ARRIVING` set.
- Decided:     The summoner's path passes through the spot without stopping. As it passes, it gives **one call
               blip**, and the station jumps in at that instant, in the same hue and with the same ring shape, so the
               two read as one cause and effect (R8, R10). The hold and the fly-back go. The ship carries on to
               its next place: its next sortie if one is waiting (E4's P4), else its rest beside its work (13 §4).
               The summoner is named from the blip (E2: plates from the act) and its plate rides with the ship
               for `NOTE_MIN_MS`. The rule's phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival (a 15 §7 row). Under
               reduced motion the ship doesn't fly: the blip and the arrival play at its place.
- Acceptance:
  - A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors.
  - A unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place, and the station's act
    starts within 50 ms of the blip.
  - 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`. The schedule goldens are updated, and the packet names each change.
  - The ledger shows the saving per pod.
- Risk:        schedule (medium: every pod with a summon).
- Touches:     `theme/starChart/maneuvers/stationJumpIn.ts`, `engine/pace.ts` (`facility.enter` phases),
               `chart/fx/commands.ts` (`pursue` passing through), 13 §6, 05 §8 (M-row of the jump-in), 15 §7.
- Depends on:  F1
- State:       open

### F3 Summon chains
- Asked:       "In the chained case ... he would basically move smoothly around the star system as stations appear in
               succession behind him (likely only fractions of a second between their activation) without [the]
               ship stopping ... Any action that summons a station within a short time period by the same captain
               (EG, same or adjacent workday OR within 30 seconds of the playback time) should just execute a
               smooth, chained maneuver like this."
- Today:       Each summon is its own `facility.enter`, and each station's first PR opening (`attachment.open`)
               waits for it. The nearest pattern is E7's Sector sweep (M-32): one carrier draft in place of many
               (`sweepCreations`, `PlannedManeuver.sweep`), revealing each piece in turn, with one note; and
               B-21/B-22's fuse, which joins raw beats into one without re-timing an event.
- Decided:     A **summon chain**: `facility.enter` drafts with one summoner, each link within `CHAIN_WINDOW_MS`
               (30 s, 15 §10) in x of the link before (a chain, so the window slides, unlike the volley's from its
               first), **or** on the same or the next working day (weekends skipped, the viewer's zone, as B-12).
               Two links or more. The links' raw beats fuse (B-21, amended: a chain's fuse may cross **one** day
               turn, F-Q1), under the same B-15 guard as `volleysOf`; a link the guard refuses starts a new chain, and nothing else
               breaks it (F-Q6). No event is re-timed (B-14) and a seek snaps to the fused beat's end state (INV-15); across a day turn, the day rule is F4's (Days). The first link
               carries one new rule, *Summons run* (`facility.run`, phases scaled by the count, like
               `sweepPhases`), in place of the links' own drafts. The ship flies one smooth path through each
               link's spot (F2), each station jumping in as it passes, `CHAIN_STEP_MS` apart at most (about
               300 ms, 15 §10); each station's tender launches with its station.
               **Visit order is proximity, not time** (decided 2026-11-06): every chain's path (F3's and F4's)
               runs one way round the system, all clockwise or all counter-clockwise, taking the next station
               along in that direction, never the next by its PR's time, so the ships move in an arc or spiral
               instead of dashing back and forth. The direction is the one that gives the shorter sweep from the
               captain's start, from the plan's places (pure in world terms, so seek and play agree; a new pure
               `chainOrder.ts` beside `sweepOrder.ts`). The stations are different pieces, so B-15 doesn't fix
               their order.
               Labels: the summoner is named; the stations come in at rest (T4) and claim no attention slots; one
               note names the count in the source's words (R9, R12; the wording is the planner's, e.g. *PRs into
               36 Repositories*). History keeps every event's row, and its *now* mark walks the visit order.
- Acceptance:
  - Unit tests: grouping is deterministic over the goldens; both window conditions chain, and F1's bounding cases
    don't (or start a new chain); no fuse crosses more than one day turn; B-15 holds; a seek into the middle of a
    chain draws exactly the stations whose links have passed.
  - `chainOrder` tests: one direction throughout, the shorter of the two sweeps, deterministic on ties.
  - An e2e case on F1's pod: the summoner's speed never drops to zero in the chain, at most four labels show, and
    every station's History row is there.
  - The ledger: F1's run's summons play in under 20 s at 1× (about 1 min 40 s today at 2.8 s each).
- Risk:        schedule (high: goldens, seek and play).
- Touches:     `engine/maneuvers.ts` (beside `sweepCreations`), `engine/director.ts` (the fuse ranges),
               `playback/schedule.ts` (`fuseRanges`), `engine/pace.ts` (`facility.run`), `stationJumpIn.ts` or a
               new `summonsRun.ts`, `chainOrder.ts` (new), `chart/fx/v1/interpreter.ts`, `packs/events.ts` (the
               note), 05 B-21 and a new M-row, 13 §6, 03 (`PlannedManeuver`), 15 §7 and §10.
- Depends on:  F2
- State:       open

# Tests, and how to iterate quickly

**Status:** current as of 2026-10-27 (through v1.3 Block B). The e2e specs and goldens are named below, and the unit tests and
drive steps mostly are; the v1.2 tests and steps are listed in the v1 table's v1.2 rows.

Decided 2026-10-07: the full e2e suite takes minutes, so iteration runs a few of its pieces, and the
full suite runs once before handing back.

| Command | What | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `npm test` | Unit and golden (Vitest) | ~5 s |
| `npm run e2e:keystone` | One path per area, tagged `@keystone`, specs in parallel | ~40 s |
| `npm run e2e:spec -- <name…>` | Named specs, e.g. `npm run e2e:spec -- explore slice4` | per spec |
| `npm run e2e` | Everything: the specs in parallel, then the pixel and frame-time specs alone | ~3 min |
| `npm run bake:asteroids` | Re-bake `assets/atlas/asteroids.{png,json}` from the procedural asteroids through the gallery (23 C7); `asteroid-atlas.spec.ts` checks the atlas path renders (no missing frames) with its flag on | seconds |
| `npm run drive -- <steps.ts>` | Launch the app, run steps, keep screenshots, state, console, and dev log | seconds |

**While iterating:** run the specs for what changed (below), plus `e2e:keystone` once things look
right. Run `npm run e2e` once before handing work back.

## Windows don't appear (decided 2026-10-09)

`npm run e2e` never shows its windows: they were opening centred, over whatever you were doing. A
hidden window still animates (`backgroundThrottling` is off in test mode) and Playwright still
composites it, so the pixel baselines and the review stills are unaffected — the whole suite passes
hidden.

- **To watch a run:** `STAR_CHART_TEST_SHOW=1 npm run e2e` (or any single spec). The window is pinned
  to the top-left of the primary display, and opens without taking focus.
- **`STAR_CHART_TEST_DPR=2`** launches with that devicePixelRatio (default 1), for checks that depend on it.

10:How to read it (decided here): **"its halcyon golden"** means two things. The Meteor scope's new entry in `sprint-pods.scenes.json`, which appears by itself. And a new Solar golden for this pod only, `halcyon-meteor.{plan,scenes}.json`, so F2 to F4 have a diff to read. **"36 stations"** are the run's 36. The pod has 37: the run's 36 plus the lone summon's station, which a single-summon case needs (a summon always brings a new station). The e2e checks that all 36 run repos are drawn and that the total is 37.
13:1. **The pod is Meteor Pod** (`Halcyon Reach\Meteor Pod`, area 8005, a favorite). The name fits a shower of 36 in a minute. Comet is hand-written, and this pod is too: a `meteor(): PodBuild` in `pods.ts`, with a loop for the 36. Item ids are 12001+ (today's highest is 11227), PR ids 21001+ (today's highest is 20764), and the new Feature is **9018 'Platform upkeep'**. Meteor goes last everywhere (areas, repos, people, events, runs), so nothing that exists moves.
14:2. **Cast.** `cast.ts` is generated, so extend `scripts/find-cast.ts` and re-run it (`npx vite-node -c vitest.config.ts scripts/find-cast.ts`). After `const comet = …`, add `const meteor = pick(8, { hulls: true, colours: true }, <fresh have sets>)`. After `cometRepo`, add `const meteorRepos = pickRepos(37, new Set(), new Set())`. Emit `METEOR_CAST` after `PULSAR_CAST` (offset 49), and `METEOR_REPOS` after `PULSAR_REPOS`. The picks are greedy over a shared `used` set, so appending them leaves every existing line byte-identical. **Check that `git diff` on cast.ts only adds lines.** The roles go by index: [0] **A**, the run's captain; [1] **B**, the other captain; [2] **C**, the second author; [3..7] **D–H**, approvers who hold no items (like Quasar's manager). `METEOR_REPOS[0..35]` are the run's repos and `[36]` is the lone summon's.
15:3. **The timeline, exactly as given.** Times are UTC and the zone is America/Los_Angeles, so every time below falls on the same local date. Every item is made at planning (Fri 11 Sep, 18:00–18:20Z) in S41/Meteor. Stories and the Bug have parent 9018, and Tasks have their Story as parent. With no creations inside the round, there is no opening sweep. When a PR opens while its item is Active, add `column(item, 'Code Review')`, as `emitItem` does. Every PR gets `prStats` from `prStatsFor(<PrPlan-shaped object>, METEOR handles)`.
17:     - **Opens:** PR `21001+i` into `METEOR_REPOS[i]`, i = 0..35, at Wed 16 17:00:00 + 1.5 s·i (the last is at 17:00:52.5). Each is titled `Move <repo> to the new base image`, links [12001], and is authored by A.
22:   - **F-Q5 station (a run link that is also an E6 volley).** C's Story 12050 'Cache the rate tables' goes Active Mon 14 17:30. Its Task 12051 goes Active Mon 14 17:35 and Closed Tue 15 19:00. PR **21040** goes into `METEOR_REPOS[35]` (the repo of run PR 21036, merged at j=5, Wed 19:25). It opens Wed 16 18:40, links [12050], and is completed by C at **the same instant, 19:25:00**, emitted just after A's merge, approvedBy [G]. 12050 goes Resolved Tue 22 18:00 and Closed Thu 24 17:00. That is more than 24 working hours after the merge, so there is no arc.
23:   - **A link the B-15 guard must refuse.** S2 12010 'Rotate the shared signing keys' goes Active Fri 18 19:30. Its Task 12011 'Rotate the staging keys' goes Active at 19:45. A opens PR 21041 into `METEOR_REPOS[3]` and PR 21042 into `[20]` on Fri 18 at 20:00 and 20:05. These go into existing stations, so they are not summons. Merges are Mon 21 at 17:00 (approvedBy [D,E]) and 17:40 (approvedBy [E,F]). **Task 12011 goes Closed Mon 21 17:20.** That is S2's only work that Monday. B-1 puts it in the first merge's beat, so the second merge's beat comes after a draft touching S2. S2 stays Active to the end, so there is no arc.
24:   - **Two merges more than a working day apart.** S3 12020 'Retire the legacy health checks' goes Active Tue 22 19:30. Its Task 12021 goes Active at 19:40. A opens PR 21043 into `METEOR_REPOS[11]` and PR 21044 into `[27]` on Tue 22 at 20:00 and 20:05. Merges are **Wed 23 18:00** (approvedBy [D,E,F]) and **Fri 25 18:00** (approvedBy [E,G]). 12021 goes Closed Fri 25 17:30, and S3 goes Resolved at 18:30 and Closed at 21:00. Every working day between A's separate merge groups (Fri 18, Tue 22, Thu 24) has a played Meteor beat. So no two groups can fuse across at most one day turn, and none can fall within 30 s in x.
25:   - **The same captain's single summon.** S4 12030 'Pin the base image in the new search service' goes Active Thu 24 18:30. Its Task 12031 goes Active at 18:35. PR **21045** goes into `METEOR_REPOS[36]` (the 37th station) on Thu 24 19:00. It **stays open** at the sprint's end: a merge would chain with Fri's. A has no other summon after Wed 16.

So the ledger's tables gain Meteor (7th, last), and C2's Candidates, the Built rows (frozen, against C2's per-pod estimates), the director golden and the engine tests over `resolvePods()` keep measuring the six they were set against. # F2 Summon on the fly: tests written first

Tests only. Nothing here implements F2. Fixture data only (INV-18): the cases are Meteor Pod (27 F1), Harbor and Nova.

## Files

- `tests/unit/summonOnTheFly.test.ts` (vitest)
- `tests/e2e/summon-on-the-fly.spec.ts` (Playwright, `parallel` project)

## Acceptance line → tests → how they fail today (at 61e4958)

| Acceptance line | Test(s) | Today |
|---|---|---|
| A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors | e2e `A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors: it plays the flight plus the arrival, no crew hold` | Fails. The cell's note gives `4835 ms`, but it should be no more than the rule's phase span (2815). The loops, the stuck count and the console-error parts pass today. |
| A unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place … | unit `the summoner's pursue has no hold … no hold, no wait, no hold command` | Fails: `holdS` 3.82 on the summoner's pursue. |
| (same) | unit `the summoner's pursue has no hold … flown, its ship never stops until it is there` | Fails: the ship stands still for 3817 ms at the spot. |
| (same) | e2e `full motion: the summoner never parks beside the station it summons, and carries on to its next place` (Meteor's lone summon in the app, captains sampled every frame) | Fails: `3811 ms still at 691.6 from the station` (the spot, 1.9 × the station's r of 364). |
| … and the station's act starts within 50 ms of the blip | unit `one call blip, in the arrival's hue and ring shape, given where the ship is` | Fails: no blip. Every jump-in effect today is drawn on the station. |
| (same) | unit `the station's act starts within 50 ms of the blip, as the ship passes the spot` | Fails: no blip. |
| (Decided: under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly; the blip and the arrival play at its place) | unit `under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly: the blip and the arrival play at its place` | Fails: no blip. |
| (same) | e2e `reduced motion: the summoner doesn't fly; the station still arrives` | **Passes today.** It's a guard: today's pursue already snaps under reduced motion. |
| 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`. The schedule goldens are updated … | unit `<pod>: every planned jump-in lasts its phases, no crew hold or fly-back past the arrival` (Meteor, Harbor, Nova) | Fails: `durationMs` is 4835, but it should be `spanMs(phases)` = 2815. The 15 §7 row itself is already enforced by `docTables.test.ts` (Length ms = the phase span), which goes red once the phases change and the row doesn't. The goldens move with the build (`-u`). The packet names the changes, so no test is written for that. |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | unit `no pod's facility.enter is charged a crew hold any more` | Fails: Nova's `facility.enter` hold is 2020 ms (Quasar 12120, Pulsar 15860, Meteor 35140 …). |
| (same) | unit `the Built section has an F2 row on all seven pods, Meteor included; …` | Fails: no `F2` rows in `buildBuilt()`. |

There is also a fixture check, `the real lone summon plans a jump-in with its summoner`, which passes. It guards the other tests' setup.

## How the unit test judges motion

The jump-in planned is the real one: Meteor Pod's lone summon (PR 21045, Thu 24 Sep 19:00Z), from
`planManeuvers`. The test plays the Star Chart choreography for `facility.enter`, found by rule id rather than by
file, on a lenient stub scene:

- Each phase runs at its `atMs` with live cast views. The ship's anchor follows where it is drawn.
- Each call is issued at its delay.
- Every move the summoner gets (`pursue`/`hold`, made by the registry's own command) runs frame by frame at 60 fps.

The test therefore judges where the ship is drawn and when, not argument names. One argument check remains: no
`holdS`/`waitS` > 0 and no `hold` command on the summoner. The *blip* is any effect that isn't a move or an act
and isn't drawn on the station. Today every jump-in effect is drawn on the station, so there are none. The
*arrival* is the act phase's effects on the station. "Same hue and ring shape" means that the arrival has a call of
the blip's command with the blip's `color`.

## Decisions (judgment calls, none answered by 27's Decisions)

1. **"No hold between its flight and its next place"** is judged as no run of more than two still frames (33 ms)
   between the ship leaving and reaching its layout target (`goalOf`), and no `holdS`/`waitS`/`hold`. An eased
   pass that slows near the spot but never stops passes.
2. **The station jumps in "at that instant"** means that, at the station's `jump` act, the ship is within 2.5 × the
   station's r of the station (the spot is 1.9 r today). Exactly one blip, within 50 ms of the act.
3. **"The blip and the arrival play at its place"** (reduced motion): the blip is drawn within one station-radius of
   the ship's unmoved place, which means it is anchored at the ship, not at the spot.
4. **"Phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival"** is read as this: the planned `facility.enter` lasts exactly its
   phases (no crew-turn extension from `crewTimes`, which made it 4835), and no longer than today's 2815. Whether
   `tell` stays is the builder's call, so it isn't pinned.
5. **The ledger's saving** is a `BUILT` row with id `F2` covering all seven pods, Meteor included (F1 measured
   Meteor "before F2", and `resolvePods` says "F2 to F4 opt in"). It must never cost time, and it must save more
   than zero on Nova, Convoy Planning, Harbor (not sped by the director) and Meteor. Comet's `facility.enter`
   holds no lead hold today, and Quasar and Pulsar are sped, so those three only need ≥ 0. A further check: no pod's
   `facility.enter` row in the ledger is charged `hold`.
6. **The e2e uses Meteor's lone summon in the app** (story time keeps it at 19:00Z), not a new fixture. The
   summoner is the captain whose drawn path comes nearest the new station. A still spell of 200 ms or more within
   3 × the station's drawn r (the hit circle, in world units) fails, unless it is where the ship ends up.
7. **Not tested** (not acceptance lines): the plate riding with the ship for `NOTE_MIN_MS`, and P4's injected
   `waitS` for a captain whose next turn follows (the interpreter adds it after the choreography). F3 covers the
   chained case.

## Existing tests the build will need to touch (heads-up, not written here)

- `tests/unit/commands.test.ts` › `Station jump-in issues no beacon, bearing or planet rings`: it expects exactly one
  ring in `gather` (the fold) and a pursue there. A blip in `gather` would change that count.
- `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` › `E1 to E5 measure what they measured before volleys`: its filter keeps every id
  that doesn't start with E6/E7/E8/E10, so an `F2` row would land in it. The committed `pacing-built.json` also has
  to be regenerated.
- 15 §8's effect-audit rows for Station jump-in, and the `docTables` `effect-audit` check.

file, on a lenient stub scene:

- Each call is issued at its delay.
- Every move the summoner gets (`pursue`/`hold`, made by the registry's own command) runs frame by frame at 60 fps.

The test therefore judges where the ship is drawn and when, not argument names. One argument check remains: no
`holdS`/`waitS` > 0 and no `hold` command on the summoner. The *blip* is any effect that isn't a move or an act
and isn't drawn on the station. Today every jump-in effect is drawn on the station, so there are none. The

# F2 Summon on the fly: tests written first

Tests only. Nothing here implements F2. Fixture data only (INV-18): the cases are Meteor Pod (27 F1), Harbor and Nova.

## Files

- `tests/unit/summonOnTheFly.test.ts` (vitest)
- `tests/e2e/summon-on-the-fly.spec.ts` (Playwright, `parallel` project)

## Acceptance line → tests → how they fail today (at 61e4958)

| Acceptance line | Test(s) | Today |
|---|---|---|
| A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors | e2e `A gallery demo cell (the jump-in cell), in full and reduced motion, with no console errors: it plays the flight plus the arrival, no crew hold` | Fails. The cell's note gives `4835 ms`, but it should be no more than the rule's phase span (2815). The loops, the stuck count and the console-error parts pass today. |
| A unit test: the summoner's pursue has no hold between its flight and its next place … | unit `the summoner's pursue has no hold … no hold, no wait, no hold command` | Fails: `holdS` 3.82 on the summoner's pursue. |
| (same) | unit `the summoner's pursue has no hold … flown, its ship never stops until it is there` | Fails: the ship stands still for 3817 ms at the spot. |
| (same) | e2e `full motion: the summoner never parks beside the station it summons, and carries on to its next place` (Meteor's lone summon in the app, captains sampled every frame) | Fails: `3811 ms still at 691.6 from the station` (the spot, 1.9 × the station's r of 364). |
| … and the station's act starts within 50 ms of the blip | unit `one call blip, in the arrival's hue and ring shape, given where the ship is` | Fails: no blip. Every jump-in effect today is drawn on the station. |
| (same) | unit `the station's act starts within 50 ms of the blip, as the ship passes the spot` | Fails: no blip. |
| (Decided: under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly; the blip and the arrival play at its place) | unit `under reduced motion the ship doesn't fly: the blip and the arrival play at its place` | Fails: no blip. |
| (same) | e2e `reduced motion: the summoner doesn't fly; the station still arrives` | **Passes today.** It's a guard: today's pursue already snaps under reduced motion. |
| 15 §7's row and `docTables.test.ts`. The schedule goldens are updated … | unit `<pod>: every planned jump-in lasts its phases, no crew hold or fly-back past the arrival` (Meteor, Harbor, Nova) | Fails: `durationMs` is 4835, but it should be `spanMs(phases)` = 2815. The 15 §7 row itself is already enforced by `docTables.test.ts` (Length ms = the phase span), which goes red once the phases change and the row doesn't. The goldens move with the build (`-u`). The packet names the changes, so no test is written for that. |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | unit `no pod's facility.enter is charged a crew hold any more` | Fails: Nova's `facility.enter` hold is 2020 ms (Quasar 12120, Pulsar 15860, Meteor 35140 …). |
| (same) | unit `the Built section has an F2 row on all seven pods, Meteor included; …` | Fails: no `F2` rows in `buildBuilt()`. |

There is also a fixture check, `the real lone summon plans a jump-in with its summoner`, which passes. It guards the other tests' setup.

## How the unit test judges motion

The jump-in planned is the real one: Meteor Pod's lone summon (PR 21045, Thu 24 Sep 19:00Z), from
`planManeuvers`. The test plays the Star Chart choreography for `facility.enter`, found by rule id rather than by
file, on a lenient stub scene:

- Each phase runs at its `atMs` with live cast views. The ship's anchor follows where it is drawn.
- Each call is issued at its delay.
- Every move the summoner gets (`pursue`/`hold`, made by the registry's own command) runs frame by frame at 60 fps.

The test therefore judges where the ship is drawn and when, not argument names. One argument check remains: no
`holdS`/`waitS` > 0 and no `hold` command on the summoner. The *blip* is any effect that isn't a move or an act
and isn't drawn on the station. Today every jump-in effect is drawn on the station, so there are none. The
*arrival* is the act phase's effects on the station. "Same hue and ring shape" means that the arrival has a call of
the blip's command with the blip's `color`.

## Decisions (judgment calls, none answered by 27's Decisions)

1. **"No hold between its flight and its next place"** is judged as no run of more than two still frames (33 ms)
   between the ship leaving and reaching its layout target (`goalOf`), and no `holdS`/`waitS`/`hold`. An eased
   pass that slows near the spot but never stops passes.
2. **The station jumps in "at that instant"** means that, at the station's `jump` act, the ship is within 2.5 × the
   station's r of the station (the spot is 1.9 r today). Exactly one blip, within 50 ms of the act.
3. **"The blip and the arrival play at its place"** (reduced motion): the blip is drawn within one station-radius of
   the ship's unmoved place, which means it is anchored at the ship, not at the spot.
4. **"Phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival"** is read as this: the planned `facility.enter` lasts exactly its
   phases (no crew-turn extension from `crewTimes`, which made it 4835), and no longer than today's 2815. Whether
   `tell` stays is the builder's call, so it isn't pinned.
5. **The ledger's saving** is a `BUILT` row with id `F2` covering all seven pods, Meteor included (F1 measured
   Meteor "before F2", and `resolvePods` says "F2 to F4 opt in"). It must never cost time, and it must save more
   than zero on Nova, Convoy Planning, Harbor (not sped by the director) and Meteor. Comet's `facility.enter`
   holds no lead hold today, and Quasar and Pulsar are sped, so those three only need ≥ 0. A further check: no pod's
   `facility.enter` row in the ledger is charged `hold`.
6. **The e2e uses Meteor's lone summon in the app** (story time keeps it at 19:00Z), not a new fixture. The
   summoner is the captain whose drawn path comes nearest the new station. A still spell of 200 ms or more within
   3 × the station's drawn r (the hit circle, in world units) fails, unless it is where the ship ends up.
7. **Not tested** (not acceptance lines): the plate riding with the ship for `NOTE_MIN_MS`, and P4's injected
   `waitS` for a captain whose next turn follows (the interpreter adds it after the choreography). F3 covers the
   chained case.

## Existing tests the build will need to touch (heads-up, not written here)

- `tests/unit/commands.test.ts` › `Station jump-in issues no beacon, bearing or planet rings`: it expects exactly one
  ring in `gather` (the fold) and a pursue there. A blip in `gather` would change that count.
- `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` › `E1 to E5 measure what they measured before volleys`: its filter keeps every id
  that doesn't start with E6/E7/E8/E10, so an `F2` row would land in it. The committed `pacing-built.json` also has
  to be regenerated.
- 15 §8's effect-audit rows for Station jump-in, and the `docTables` `effect-audit` check.

# F2 Summon on the fly: review 1

**Verdict: changes requested.** The acceptance lines the tests pin are met honestly, and the checks pass. Two
Decided behaviours aren't built: the ship doesn't carry on to a waiting next sortie (P4), and a captain new to the
scene loses its jump-in. The riding plate also outlives the attention budget's hold (R14). None of these is
tested, so the green suite doesn't cover them.

## Checks run
- `npm run -s typecheck`: clean. `npm run -s lint`: clean.
- `npm test`: 110 files, 1730 tests passed.
- `npx electron-vite build`, then `npx playwright test tests/e2e/summon-on-the-fly.spec.ts tests/e2e/gallery-assets.spec.ts`: 7/7 passed (the jump-in cell in full and reduced motion with no console errors; Meteor's lone summon in full and reduced motion).
- A probe script, kept outside the repo in `/tmp`: for every pod's planned beats, the `facility.enter` plays to which `nearWaits` gives the summoner a P4 wait (results under M1).

## Acceptance
| Line | Met? |
|---|---|
| Gallery jump-in cell, full and reduced motion, no console errors | Yes (e2e passes; the cell lasts the phases, 2815 ms). |
| Unit: no hold between flight and next place; the station's act within 50 ms of the blip | Yes, by construction: the blip is the act's first call at delay 0, beside `act jump`. Not gamed: the test simulates the real `Flyby` frame by frame. |
| 15 §7 row and `docTables`; schedule goldens updated, the packet names each change | Partly (m2, m3). The row's text changed and its Length didn't. The goldens' changes aren't each named. |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | Yes for short+montage levers. With every lever the saving isn't shown (m4). |

## Test changes: judgement
- `tests/unit/commands.test.ts`: justified. The old assertions pinned the gather fold ring, which F2 removes on purpose: the blip replaces it, and 15 §8's audit row is replaced to match. The new assertions are stricter: `pass === true`, no `holdS`, and two act rings. The Shuttle tender check is unchanged, with only its variable renamed.
- `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` filter `!x.id.startsWith('F')`: justified. `BEFORE_VOLLEYS` holds only E1 to E5 rows, and the F2 row is new. The committed rows E1 to E10 in `pacing-built.json` are byte-identical: the diff only appends seven F2 rows. That's because the pre-F2 items run with `held()`, which follows the precedent of `sweeps`, `rises` and `late` (E7, E8, E10).
- `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json`: the regeneration is genuine. Only the director's estimates and tempo move, and no other schedule golden carries a `facility.enter`. Not every change is a saving, though (m3).

## Findings

### M1 (Major): the summoner never carries on to a waiting next sortie; the P4 wait is dropped silently
`src/renderer/src/chart/fx/commands.ts:367`
```ts
if (a.pass) return new Flyby(scene, a.pk, start, live(a.to), live(a.look ?? a.to), a.durS, a.backS ?? a.durS, a.wake ?? 0);
```
The interpreter still injects P4's `waitS` into the summoner's pursue (`interpreter.ts:700-703`, via `nearWaits`, which now releases at `workEndOf`). `Flyby` ignores it, so the ship always flies to `goalOf` (its rest) and then flies out again for its next turn. Decided says: "The ship carries on to its next place: its next sortie if one is waiting (E4's P4), else its rest beside its work." build.md Decision 3 admits this isn't built and isn't pinned by a test.
Evidence (the probe, `nearWaits` over every pod's planned beats): Meteor has 37 summons, and **34** give the summoner a P4 wait. Pulsar has 9 summons, and 1 gets a wait. In those cases the ship passes the spot, glides home over 0.8 s, sits, and flies back out: the stop-and-go the item exists to remove. F3 will chain Meteor's same-captain summons, but F2's Decided covers the single case now, and Pulsar's single case isn't a chain.
**Fix:** when the summoner has a P4 wait, the pass's on-leg should end at its next sortie's spot, or the next sortie should take over from where the ship is drawn without flying home first. One way: `Flyby` honours `waitS` by easing to a stop near the spot. Better: hand off to the next turn. Add a unit test.

### M2 (Major): a captain new to the scene this beat loses its jump-in; it is hidden through the flight
`src/renderer/src/chart/fx/commands.ts:367` (the `pass` branch returns before `scene.takeJump(a.pk)`). `Sortie` received `scene.takeJump(a.pk)` and dropped the guest out of hyperspace at its spot (K-13, 22 C8). The `Flyby` path never takes the jump. The interpreter's jumpers (`interpreter.ts:504-545`) are captains not in `ctx.before`. Each has `scene.markJump(pk)`, which calls `fadeView(pk, 0)`, so it stays invisible while the `Flyby` moves it. At gather + 0.6 s the fallback fires (`if (!scene.takeJump(pk)) return;` fails to return because the jump is still pending). It then issues the rest entrance or a `FadeIn`, mid-flight and while the `Flyby` owns the node. The result: the blip is given at a ship that is invisible or only half faded in, and two movers place one node.
**Fix:** in the `pass` branch, `if (scene.takeJump(a.pk))`, either jump in at the spot and then carry on, or fall back to the `Sortie` jump path. Add a unit or e2e case with a summoner new to the beat.

### M3 (Major): the riding plate outlives the budget's hold (R14)
`src/renderer/src/chart/fx/v1/interpreter.ts:621`
```ts
const crew = onFly ? { openMs: claimMs(m.phases), closeMs: claimMs(m.phases) + Math.max(NOTE_MIN_MS, CREW_FOLD_MS + CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS + 250) } : crewTimes(m.phases);
```
The plate is whole from 1015 to 3285 ms and folds until about 3805 ms. The planner's attention hold is `heldMs = max(durMs, NOTE_MIN_MS)` (`maneuvers.ts:619`), which is now 2815 because `durMs` no longer includes `crewTimes().leaveMs`. So for about 1 s, the planner counts places as free while this plate still shows. A crowded beat can then show `ATTENTION_MAX + 1` labels (R14, 22 C10). The interpreter can over-run the budget this way because it no longer agrees with the planner. Before F2, `durMs` covered `leaveMs`, so the two matched.
**Fix:** derive one window, used by both the planner (`heldMs`, or the draft's `durMs`) and the interpreter, for example a shared `flyCrewTimes(phases)` in `maneuvers.ts`. Name its value in 15 §10 rather than writing a bare `+ 250`.

### m1 (Minor): the doc and the code disagree on the plate's length, and R8 and the shut-in-flight rule have no carve-out
- 13 §6 (`docs/13-game-design.md:685`) and the `PaceRule.onTheFly` comment (`pace.ts:87`) say the plate rides for `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1800 ms). The code uses 2270 ms, built from an unnamed 250 ms. This departs from Decided ("for `NOTE_MIN_MS`"). The departure is in build.md but not in the docs, and it isn't flagged for the block note.
- 15's `CREW_FOLD_MS` row says the plate is "shut in flight" (`Sortie.crewOpen`). `rides` overrides that (`castLabels.ts:107`) with no note in the row.
- R8 ("movement and interaction never blur into one", 13 §1) is now contradicted by design (the call is given in flight). The departure was the user's decision, but 13 §1 should note it.
**Fix:** make the docs match the code, or the code match `NOTE_MIN_MS` after M3. Add the exceptions to the 15 row and to R8.

### m2 (Minor): "the rule's phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival" is read as "the length stays the phases'"
`src/shared/engine/pace.ts:520`. The phases are unchanged (tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600), so 15 §7's Length row didn't move. The acceptance's "15 §7's row" implies that it does. The 300 ms tell (a ring before the ship moves) is neither flight nor arrival. tests.md Decision 4 leaves tell to the builder, so this isn't a test failure, but it is a reading of the Decided that should be confirmed. **Fix:** confirm with the user or the block note that tell stays, or drop it (saving 300 ms per summon) and update the 15 §7 Length.

### m3 (Minor): build.md doesn't name each golden change, and one of them is a cost
`tests/golden/__golden__/director.json`: Quasar's `estimateMs` goes **296189 → 298283 (+2.1 s)** with tempo 1.9 → 1.8. Pulsar's goes 294434 → 287015 with tempo 1.1 → 1.05. build.md says only "Comet 53065 -> 51045 etc." The acceptance asks that "the packet names each change". **Fix:** list each pod's estimate and tempo change in build.md. Explain why Quasar's directed estimate grows: speed relaxes, so the target re-fits.

### m4 (Minor): the ledger shows only the short+montage saving; the app's own (every lever) is hidden
`scripts/pacing-built.ts:148`. The F2 row follows E6's lever restriction, which is fine as a precedent. E6, however, also has `E6+` ("with every lever") beside it, and F2 has none. build.md records that with every lever Pulsar is −3908 ms, a cost, and that number appears nowhere in the ledger. **Fix:** add an `F2+` row with every lever, as E6+ does, so the ledger shows what the app plays.

### n1 (Nit): dead parameter and wasted work in the `pass` path
- `Flyby` takes `look` (`movers.ts:247`) and never reads it.
- In `commands.ts:366-367`, `to` (with `clearOfPlate`) is computed before the `pass` branch, which then ignores it and calls `live(a.to)` again.
- `holdS` and `waitS` are dropped without a trace when `pass` is set; at least a comment, and see M1.

### n2 (Nit): `onTheFly(id)` duplicates `ruleById`
`src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:800` searches `PACE_RULES` again. `ruleById(id)?.onTheFly` is already used in the interpreter. The module stays pure: no Electron, DOM or Pixi imports were added to `src/shared/`.

### n3 (Nit): `PASS_ON_S = 0.8` is a timing literal outside 15
`stationJumpIn.ts`. It's the old fly-back literal under a new name, and 13 §6 states 0.8 s. A 15 §7 or §10 mention would keep "values live in 15" whole.

## Not found
- No Pixi v7 idioms: `Flyby` reuses `Streak` and `Graphics`-free drawing.
- No real data and no PAT use.
- Reduced motion is as Decided: the pursue snaps, and the blip and arrival play at the ship's place (unit and e2e).
- The other pods' committed Built rows are unchanged.

- **M3 (Major), `interpreter.ts:621`:** The plate stays open until about 3.8 s from the start, folding included. The planner holds the attention slot only until 2815 ms, because `durMs` no longer includes the crew's leave time. That leaves about 1 s in which a crowded beat could show one label over `ATTENTION_MAX`, against R14. The plate length also uses an unnamed `+ 250` ms.

- **m2 (Minor):** The phases are unchanged, so "the phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival" is read as the length staying at the phases' 2815 ms. The 300 ms tell stays, and 15 §7's Length doesn't move. This reading needs confirming.

- **n2 (Nit):** `onTheFly()` repeats a lookup that `ruleById` already does. `src/shared/` stays pure.
- **n3 (Nit):** `PASS_ON_S = 0.8` is a timing literal with no row in 15.

**Nothing found on:** Pixi v8 idioms, real data or PAT use, `src/shared/` purity, or reduced motion, which behaves as Decided. The other items' committed ledger rows are unchanged.

The full review is in `/Users/amorgan/sluice-bench/F2/A4-2/clone/docs/progress/v1.4/work/F2/review.md`.

**Checks:** typecheck and lint are clean, `npm test` passes (1730 tests), and after `electron-vite build` the e2e specs `summon-on-the-fly` and `gallery-assets` pass 7/7. I also ran a throwaway probe script from `/tmp` (nothing added to the repo).

**Test changes:** all three are justified.
- `commands.test.ts`: F2 removes the fold ring on purpose, and the new assertions are stricter.
- `pacingBuilt.test.ts`: the extra `F` exclusion is fine, since the earlier E rows in `pacing-built.json` are byte-identical and the diff only appends seven F2 rows.
- `director.json`: the regeneration is genuine.

**Findings:**
- **M1 (Major), `commands.ts:367`:** The fly-by mover (`Flyby`) ignores the `waitS` that the interpreter still injects for the "captain waits near" rule (E4's P4). So the ship always flies home, then flies out again for its next turn. The Decided says it should carry on to its next sortie if one is waiting. In the probe, 34 of Meteor's 37 summons and 1 of Pulsar's 9 have such a wait. The builder's own record says this isn't built and isn't tested.
- **M2 (Major), `commands.ts:367`:** The `pass` branch never calls `scene.takeJump`. A captain who is new to the scene in that beat stays hidden through the flight. Then the fallback entrance or fade-in fires mid-flight, while the `Flyby` is still moving the ship. The blip plays at an invisible or half-faded ship.
- **M3 (Major), `interpreter.ts:621`:** The plate stays open until about 3.8 s from the start, folding included. The planner holds the attention slot only until 2815 ms, because `durMs` no longer includes the crew's leave time. That leaves about 1 s in which a crowded beat could show one label over `ATTENTION_MAX`, against R14. The plate length also uses an unnamed `+ 250` ms.
- **m1 (Minor):** Doc and code disagree:
  - 13 §6 and the `pace.ts` comment say the plate lasts `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1800 ms); the code uses 2270 ms.
  - 15's `CREW_FOLD_MS` row still says the plate is "shut in flight".
  - R8 ("movement and interaction never blur") needs a note for this departure.
- **m2 (Minor):** The phases are unchanged, so "the phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival" is read as the length staying at the phases' 2815 ms. The 300 ms tell stays, and 15 §7's Length doesn't move. This reading needs confirming.
- **m3 (Minor):** `build.md` doesn't name each golden change. One is a cost: Quasar's directed estimate grows from 296189 to 298283 ms (+2.1 s) as its tempo drops from 1.9 to 1.8. Pulsar's tempo goes from 1.1 to 1.05.
- **m4 (Minor):** The F2 ledger row runs short forms and montage only. E6 has an every-lever companion (`E6+`) and F2 has none, so the cost the builder recorded with every lever on (Pulsar −3908 ms) appears nowhere in the ledger.
- **n1 (Nit):** `Flyby`'s `look` parameter is never read, and `to` (with `clearOfPlate`) is computed before the `pass` branch ignores it.
- **n2 (Nit):** `onTheFly()` repeats a lookup that `ruleById` already does. `src/shared/` stays pure.
- **n3 (Nit):** `PASS_ON_S = 0.8` is a timing literal with no row in 15.

**Nothing found on:** Pixi v8 idioms, real data or PAT use, `src/shared/` purity, or reduced motion, which behaves as Decided. The other items' committed ledger rows are unchanged.

# F2 Summon on the fly: review 1

**Verdict: changes requested.** The acceptance lines the tests pin are met honestly, and the checks pass. Two
Decided behaviours aren't built: the ship doesn't carry on to a waiting next sortie (P4), and a captain new to the
scene loses its jump-in. The riding plate also outlives the attention budget's hold (R14). None of these is
tested, so the green suite doesn't cover them.

## Checks run
- `npm run -s typecheck`: clean. `npm run -s lint`: clean.
- `npm test`: 110 files, 1730 tests passed.
- `npx electron-vite build`, then `npx playwright test tests/e2e/summon-on-the-fly.spec.ts tests/e2e/gallery-assets.spec.ts`: 7/7 passed (the jump-in cell in full and reduced motion with no console errors; Meteor's lone summon in full and reduced motion).
- A probe script, kept outside the repo in `/tmp`: for every pod's planned beats, the `facility.enter` plays to which `nearWaits` gives the summoner a P4 wait (results under M1).

## Acceptance
| Line | Met? |
|---|---|
| Gallery jump-in cell, full and reduced motion, no console errors | Yes (e2e passes; the cell lasts the phases, 2815 ms). |
| Unit: no hold between flight and next place; the station's act within 50 ms of the blip | Yes, by construction: the blip is the act's first call at delay 0, beside `act jump`. Not gamed: the test simulates the real `Flyby` frame by frame. |
| 15 §7 row and `docTables`; schedule goldens updated, the packet names each change | Partly (m2, m3). The row's text changed and its Length didn't. The goldens' changes aren't each named. |
| The ledger shows the saving per pod | Yes for short+montage levers. With every lever the saving isn't shown (m4). |

## Test changes: judgement
- `tests/unit/commands.test.ts`: justified. The old assertions pinned the gather fold ring, which F2 removes on purpose: the blip replaces it, and 15 §8's audit row is replaced to match. The new assertions are stricter: `pass === true`, no `holdS`, and two act rings. The Shuttle tender check is unchanged, with only its variable renamed.
- `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` filter `!x.id.startsWith('F')`: justified. `BEFORE_VOLLEYS` holds only E1 to E5 rows, and the F2 row is new. The committed rows E1 to E10 in `pacing-built.json` are byte-identical: the diff only appends seven F2 rows. That's because the pre-F2 items run with `held()`, which follows the precedent of `sweeps`, `rises` and `late` (E7, E8, E10).
- `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json`: the regeneration is genuine. Only the director's estimates and tempo move, and no other schedule golden carries a `facility.enter`. Not every change is a saving, though (m3).

## Findings

### M1 (Major): the summoner never carries on to a waiting next sortie; the P4 wait is dropped silently
`src/renderer/src/chart/fx/commands.ts:367`
```ts
if (a.pass) return new Flyby(scene, a.pk, start, live(a.to), live(a.look ?? a.to), a.durS, a.backS ?? a.durS, a.wake ?? 0);
```
The interpreter still injects P4's `waitS` into the summoner's pursue (`interpreter.ts:700-703`, via `nearWaits`, which now releases at `workEndOf`). `Flyby` ignores it, so the ship always flies to `goalOf` (its rest) and then flies out again for its next turn. Decided says: "The ship carries on to its next place: its next sortie if one is waiting (E4's P4), else its rest beside its work." build.md Decision 3 admits this isn't built and isn't pinned by a test.
Evidence (the probe, `nearWaits` over every pod's planned beats): Meteor has 37 summons, and **34** give the summoner a P4 wait. Pulsar has 9 summons, and 1 gets a wait. In those cases the ship passes the spot, glides home over 0.8 s, sits, and flies back out: the stop-and-go the item exists to remove. F3 will chain Meteor's same-captain summons, but F2's Decided covers the single case now, and Pulsar's single case isn't a chain.
**Fix:** when the summoner has a P4 wait, the pass's on-leg should end at its next sortie's spot, or the next sortie should take over from where the ship is drawn without flying home first. One way: `Flyby` honours `waitS` by easing to a stop near the spot. Better: hand off to the next turn. Add a unit test.

### M2 (Major): a captain new to the scene this beat loses its jump-in; it is hidden through the flight
`src/renderer/src/chart/fx/commands.ts:367` (the `pass` branch returns before `scene.takeJump(a.pk)`). `Sortie` received `scene.takeJump(a.pk)` and dropped the guest out of hyperspace at its spot (K-13, 22 C8). The `Flyby` path never takes the jump. The interpreter's jumpers (`interpreter.ts:504-545`) are captains not in `ctx.before`. Each has `scene.markJump(pk)`, which calls `fadeView(pk, 0)`, so it stays invisible while the `Flyby` moves it. At gather + 0.6 s the fallback fires (`if (!scene.takeJump(pk)) return;` fails to return because the jump is still pending). It then issues the rest entrance or a `FadeIn`, mid-flight and while the `Flyby` owns the node. The result: the blip is given at a ship that is invisible or only half faded in, and two movers place one node.
**Fix:** in the `pass` branch, `if (scene.takeJump(a.pk))`, either jump in at the spot and then carry on, or fall back to the `Sortie` jump path. Add a unit or e2e case with a summoner new to the beat.

### M3 (Major): the riding plate outlives the budget's hold (R14)
`src/renderer/src/chart/fx/v1/interpreter.ts:621`
```ts
const crew = onFly ? { openMs: claimMs(m.phases), closeMs: claimMs(m.phases) + Math.max(NOTE_MIN_MS, CREW_FOLD_MS + CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS + 250) } : crewTimes(m.phases);
```
The plate is whole from 1015 to 3285 ms and folds until about 3805 ms. The planner's attention hold is `heldMs = max(durMs, NOTE_MIN_MS)` (`maneuvers.ts:619`), which is now 2815 because `durMs` no longer includes `crewTimes().leaveMs`. So for about 1 s, the planner counts places as free while this plate still shows. A crowded beat can then show `ATTENTION_MAX + 1` labels (R14, 22 C10). The interpreter can over-run the budget this way because it no longer agrees with the planner. Before F2, `durMs` covered `leaveMs`, so the two matched.
**Fix:** derive one window, used by both the planner (`heldMs`, or the draft's `durMs`) and the interpreter, for example a shared `flyCrewTimes(phases)` in `maneuvers.ts`. Name its value in 15 §10 rather than writing a bare `+ 250`.

### m1 (Minor): the doc and the code disagree on the plate's length, and R8 and the shut-in-flight rule have no carve-out
- 13 §6 (`docs/13-game-design.md:685`) and the `PaceRule.onTheFly` comment (`pace.ts:87`) say the plate rides for `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1800 ms). The code uses 2270 ms, built from an unnamed 250 ms. This departs from Decided ("for `NOTE_MIN_MS`"). The departure is in build.md but not in the docs, and it isn't flagged for the block note.
- 15's `CREW_FOLD_MS` row says the plate is "shut in flight" (`Sortie.crewOpen`). `rides` overrides that (`castLabels.ts:107`) with no note in the row.
- R8 ("movement and interaction never blur into one", 13 §1) is now contradicted by design (the call is given in flight). The departure was the user's decision, but 13 §1 should note it.
**Fix:** make the docs match the code, or the code match `NOTE_MIN_MS` after M3. Add the exceptions to the 15 row and to R8.

### m2 (Minor): "the rule's phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival" is read as "the length stays the phases'"
`src/shared/engine/pace.ts:520`. The phases are unchanged (tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600), so 15 §7's Length row didn't move. The acceptance's "15 §7's row" implies that it does. The 300 ms tell (a ring before the ship moves) is neither flight nor arrival. tests.md Decision 4 leaves tell to the builder, so this isn't a test failure, but it is a reading of the Decided that should be confirmed. **Fix:** confirm with the user or the block note that tell stays, or drop it (saving 300 ms per summon) and update the 15 §7 Length.

### m3 (Minor): build.md doesn't name each golden change, and one of them is a cost
`tests/golden/__golden__/director.json`: Quasar's `estimateMs` goes **296189 → 298283 (+2.1 s)** with tempo 1.9 → 1.8. Pulsar's goes 294434 → 287015 with tempo 1.1 → 1.05. build.md says only "Comet 53065 -> 51045 etc." The acceptance asks that "the packet names each change". **Fix:** list each pod's estimate and tempo change in build.md. Explain why Quasar's directed estimate grows: speed relaxes, so the target re-fits.

### m4 (Minor): the ledger shows only the short+montage saving; the app's own (every lever) is hidden
`scripts/pacing-built.ts:148`. The F2 row follows E6's lever restriction, which is fine as a precedent. E6, however, also has `E6+` ("with every lever") beside it, and F2 has none. build.md records that with every lever Pulsar is −3908 ms, a cost, and that number appears nowhere in the ledger. **Fix:** add an `F2+` row with every lever, as E6+ does, so the ledger shows what the app plays.

### n1 (Nit): dead parameter and wasted work in the `pass` path
- `Flyby` takes `look` (`movers.ts:247`) and never reads it.
- In `commands.ts:366-367`, `to` (with `clearOfPlate`) is computed before the `pass` branch, which then ignores it and calls `live(a.to)` again.
- `holdS` and `waitS` are dropped without a trace when `pass` is set; at least a comment, and see M1.

### n2 (Nit): `onTheFly(id)` duplicates `ruleById`
`src/shared/engine/maneuvers.ts:800` searches `PACE_RULES` again. `ruleById(id)?.onTheFly` is already used in the interpreter. The module stays pure: no Electron, DOM or Pixi imports were added to `src/shared/`.

### n3 (Nit): `PASS_ON_S = 0.8` is a timing literal outside 15
`stationJumpIn.ts`. It's the old fly-back literal under a new name, and 13 §6 states 0.8 s. A 15 §7 or §10 mention would keep "values live in 15" whole.

## Not found
- No Pixi v7 idioms: `Flyby` reuses `Streak` and `Graphics`-free drawing.
- No real data and no PAT use.
- Reduced motion is as Decided: the pursue snaps, and the blip and arrival play at the ship's place (unit and e2e).
- The other pods' committed Built rows are unchanged.
# F2 Summon on the fly: build record

## What was built
- The summoner's `pursue` now has a `pass` mode (new `Flyby` mover in `chart/fx/movers.ts`): it flies out to the spot beside the station, speeding up, and carries on to its layout target without stopping (slowing only on arriving home). No `holdS`, no `waitS`, no fly-back.
- `stationJumpIn.ts`: gather is the passing `pursue` (0.715 s to the spot, 0.8 s on from it); the fold ring that repeated the flight is gone. The act gives **one call blip** (a `ring` in `HERO_GLOW`, same hue and ring shape as the station's own bloom, anchored at the ship via `a.at`) at delay 0, the same instant as `act jump`. Under reduced motion `pursue` snaps (skipped), so the blip and the arrival play at the ship's place. The guest (no ship) case is unchanged except its stay is gather + act + 600 (was gather + crew hold + 600).
- `PaceRule.onTheFly` (new, `pace.ts`, set on `facility.enter`): the planner no longer stretches the maneuver to the crew's turn (`durMs` = `spanMs(phases)` = 2815), and its release is the work's end (`releaseOf`, `releaseOfPlay`). New `onTheFly(id)` helper in `maneuvers.ts`; the gallery cell uses it.
- Plate: the interpreter names the summoner from the act (the blip) for `max(NOTE_MIN_MS, CREW_FOLD_MS + CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS + 250)` = 2270 ms, riding with the ship (`showCrew(..., rides)`; `castLabels.crew` doesn't gate a riding plate on a `Sortie`).
- Phases are unchanged (tell 300, gather 715, act 1200, land 600 = 2815): the saving is the crew hold and fly-back leaving the length (4835 -> 2815), so 15 §7's Length (2815) did not change; its "What you see" text did.
- Ledger: `scripts/pacing-built.ts` has an `F2` item on all seven pods (`allPods`), `flies`, directed with short+montage only (as E6) so adaptive speed does not re-fit the saving away (with every lever Pulsar went -3908 ms: the director relaxes its tempo). Items built before F2 now run with the summoner held (`flies` unset), so their committed rows stay as measured. Saved: Comet 0, Nova 2020, Quasar 12120, Pulsar 16160, Convoy 6060, Harbor 2420, Meteor 25644 ms.
- Docs: 15 §7 row, 15 §8 effect-audit (fold row replaced by the call-blip row), 13 §6 rows (Station jump-in, Station), 05 M-13 and T-1, 03 (`PaceRule.onTheFly`).

## Decisions (judgment calls)
1. Blip placed in `act` at delay 0 (not in gather), so it is the same instant as `act jump` by construction. Fold ring dropped (the blip is the call).
2. Phases kept as they were; "phases shrink to flight plus arrival" is met by the length being the phases'.
3. P4 (`nearWaits`) stays-near does not apply to a flyby; a next sortie takes over from where the ship is drawn (movers never jump). Not pinned by a test.
4. Plate window lengthened beyond NOTE_MIN_MS so it is whole >= CREW_OPEN_MIN_MS (an existing solar-dense test needs that of every named turn; at exactly NOTE_MIN_MS it measured 1231 ms whole, at +0 1397).
5. F2 ledger row runs short+montage levers only (see above).

## Test changes (none weakens the F2 tests)
- `tests/unit/commands.test.ts` "Station jump-in issues no beacon...": gather now has no ring (fold repeat gone) and a `pass` pursue with no hold; the act has two rings (blip + bloom). The Shuttle tender assertion is unchanged (variable renamed `tenderAct`). Reason: heads-up in tests.md; the old assertions pinned the fold ring that F2 removes.
- `tests/unit/pacingBuilt.test.ts` "E1 to E5 ...": filter also excludes ids starting `F` (the F2 row). Its committed values are untouched.
- `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json` regenerated (`-u`): the director's estimates/tempo move because every summon is 2.0 s shorter (Comet 53065 -> 51045 etc.).
- `docs/progress/v1.4/pacing-{built,candidates,ledger}.json/.md` regenerated with `npm run pacing -- --candidates`.
- No e2e spec changed.

## Checks
- `npm run -s typecheck`: clean. `npm run -s lint`: clean.
- `npm test`: 110 files, 1730 tests passed (includes summonOnTheFly 11/11, docTables, literalFence, pacingBuilt).
- e2e (after `electron-vite build`): summon-on-the-fly 3/3, gallery-assets 4/4, solar-play, montage-names, slice3a, solar, solar-dense passed; `npm run e2e:keystone` 43/43.
- Flaky, not F2: `solar-dense` "facing follows motion" fails under load (`--repeat-each=3`: six ships "wrong" at one playhead, a camera move) identically on the unmodified baseline (HEAD, built in a scratch worktree: 2 to 5 wrong of 34 to 41); it passes alone. `solar` Meteor "VC-3 at 1024x640" failed once and passed on retry.
- Full `npm run e2e` not run.

## Fix (review 1)

### M1: the summoner carries on to a waiting next sortie
- `Flyby` (`movers.ts`) now takes `waitS`. With none it flies the two legs as before. With a P4 wait it eases to a stop a little way on from the spot (`WAIT_COAST`, 35% of the way home), stays there, and only then goes home; the next sortie's `pursue` replaces the mover and starts from where the ship is drawn, so it never flies home and out again. `commands.ts` hands `waitS` to the `Flyby`.
- The interpreter's P4 wait is counted from the work's release, but a fly-by finishes its legs earlier (gather + 1.5 s against a release at the work's end). For a `pass` pursue it adds the gap (`releaseOfPlay - gatherAtOf - durS - backS`), so the ship is still parked when the next sortie sets off.
- Tests (`tests/unit/summonOnTheFlyFix.test.ts`): no wait goes home and ends; a wait of 2 s parks away from both the spot and home through the wait, then goes home; no frame jumps.

### M2: a new captain's jump-in
- The `pass` branch now calls `scene.takeJump(a.pk)`. A summoner new to the scene drops out of hyperspace at the spot (hidden, fades in over the last `JUMP_IN_S` of the out leg, no flight out) and then carries on. It is fully in as the act's blip is given. `destroy` leaves the view fully faded in.
- Tests: the jump is taken once, the ship is hidden at the start, sits at the spot (never flies out), is in by the call, and goes home after. A captain already here is shown and flies out.

### M3: the plate and the attention hold agree
- New `flyCrewTimes(phases)` in `maneuvers.ts`: the plate opens at the claim (the act) and lasts one naming turn, `VOLLEY_TURN_MS` (2540 ms: unfurl, 1500 ms whole, fold), so it is whole as long as any named turn (what the old `+ 250` bought) with no new constant. The interpreter's plate and the planner's `heldMs` (for an `onTheFly` rule that attends) both read it, so the budget holds the place until the plate is gone. The bare `+ 250` is gone. The plate is now 2540 ms, not 2270 ms, from the act.
- Tests: `flyCrewTimes` is the claim plus `VOLLEY_TURN_MS`; the beat holding the lone summon stays open until the plate is gone (`shapeOf(...).durationMs >= start + goneMs`; it was 2815 ms before the fix).

### m1, n1, n2, n3, m4
- m1: 13 §6 (Station jump-in) and 13 §1 R8 now state the decided exception, the plate's one-turn window (longer than `NOTE_MIN_MS`, as a departure from Decided, and why), the P4 wait and the K-13 jump. 15 `CREW_FOLD_MS` row names the exception to "shut in flight". `PaceRule.onTheFly` comment matches.
- n1: `Flyby` now reads `look` (it faces a jumping-in captain); `to`/`clearOfPlate` is no longer computed in the `pass` path; the `pass` doc says what `holdS`/`waitS` mean there.
- n2: `onTheFly(id)` uses `ruleById`.
- n3: 15 §10 row `PASS_ON_S` (unguarded) for the 0.8 s leg on, with `WAIT_COAST`.
- m4: an `F2+` ledger row (every lever) in `scripts/pacing-built.ts`. With the plate's hold the app's own saving is no longer a cost: Pulsar +0.2 s (it was -3.9 s), Quasar +3.8 s, Meteor +6.1 s. Ledger files regenerated (`npm run pacing -- --candidates`); the F2 row's savings are unchanged (Nova 2.0, Quasar 12.1, Pulsar 16.2, Convoy 6.1, Harbor 2.4, Meteor 25.6 s).
- m2 (the 300 ms tell stays) is a reading for the user to confirm; not changed. m3: the director golden's changes, per pod (estimate ms, tempo): Comet 53065 -> 51045; Nova 188375 -> 186355; Quasar 296189 -> 296041 (tempo 1.9 -> 1.85: speed relaxes as the pod is shorter, so the target re-fits); Pulsar 294434 -> 291949 (1.1 -> 1.05); Convoy 187265 -> 181205; Harbor 199565 -> 193505. (Before this fix Quasar read 298283 at tempo 1.8, a +2.1 s cost; the plate's hold moved it.)

### Test changes
- New: `tests/unit/summonOnTheFlyFix.test.ts` (7 tests, M1 to M3). Existing F2 tests are unchanged.
- `tests/golden/__golden__/director.json` regenerated again (above).
- `tests/e2e/solar-dense.spec.ts` "a captain's turn: named once parked ...": the summoner's riding plate is now left out of the *parked* judgement (episodes whose plate carries `data-rides`, set by `labels.ts` from the crew entry's new `rides` flag). Why: the test demands that a named ship does not travel, and F2's Decided is that the summoner's plate rides with a passing ship (a Linked PR summon moved 10 to 25 px with the plate open; it passes at HEAD, where the summoner parks). The rest of the test is not weakened: other turns still need whole >= 1.4 s and drift < 12 px, and the summoners' samples still count in the over-work and plate-flip checks.

### Checks
- `npm run -s typecheck`, `npm run -s lint`: clean. `npm test`: 111 files, 1737 tests passed.
- After `electron-vite build`: summon-on-the-fly, gallery-assets, solar-play, montage-names, slice3a, solar, solar-dense all passed; `npm run e2e:keystone` 43/43.

The interpreter also adds the gap between the fly-by's legs ending and the work's release, so the ship is still parked when the next sortie sets off.
- **M2 (jump-in):** the `pass` branch now calls `scene.takeJump`. A captain new to the scene drops out of hyperspace at the spot, fades in by the call, then carries on.

  - **Departure from Decided:** the window is 2540 ms, not `NOTE_MIN_MS` (1800). It is longer so the plate is whole at least as long as any named turn. This is documented in 13 §6 and the 15 `CREW_FOLD_MS` row.
- **Cheap findings:**
  - m1: 13 §6, 13 §1 R8 and the 15 `CREW_FOLD_MS` row now state the exceptions.
  - n1: the dead `look` parameter is now used, and `to` is no longer computed on the `pass` path.
  - n2: `onTheFly` uses `ruleById`.
  - n3: 15 has an unguarded `PASS_ON_S` row.
  - m4: added an `F2+` (every lever) ledger row. Pulsar's saving moved from -3.9 s to +0.2 s.
  - m3: the per-pod golden changes are listed in build.md.
  - m2 (does the 300 ms tell stay?) is left for the user to confirm.

- `npm run -s typecheck`: clean. `npm run -s lint`: clean. `npm test`: 111 files, 1737 tests passed.

F2 is built and committed on `bench` in two commits, nothing pushed: `5946400` (bench: tests) and `6ae2058` (sluice(F2): Summon on the fly). The working tree is clean. **The four e2e failures.** The fixing agent judged none of them to come from F2:
- **perf "p95 frame time" (Pulsar):** it also fails on an unmodified build, at 25 ms against a limit of 18.6. It looks like this machine is too slow for that check.
- **solar Meteor "VC-3 at 1024×640", solar-dense "facing follows motion" and demo "Halcyon five pods":** each fails only when the machine is loaded. Each passes when run alone or on retry, and the whole demo spec passes alone (15/15).

**How it went:**
1. **Test writer (Opus):** turned each acceptance line into unit tests and e2e checks that read what the app draws, and confirmed they failed on the old tree because the feature was missing. One reduced-motion check already passed; it only guards against a regression.
2. **Builder (Sonnet):** the summoner now flies past the station to its next place without stopping. A single call blip replaces the fold ring. A summon now lasts 2815 ms instead of 4835, and the pacing ledger gets an F2 row on all seven pods.
3. **Reviewer (Opus):** asked for changes, with three Majors:
   - When the next sortie was already waiting, the ship still flew home and back out (34 of Meteor's 37 summons).
   - A captain new to the scene stayed hidden and then faded in mid-flight.
   - The captain's name plate stayed up about 1 s after its slot in the on-screen label limit ended, against R14.

   The reviewer judged the builder's changes to existing tests justified.
4. **Second builder (Sonnet):** fixed all three Majors, added 7 unit tests that would have caught them, fixed most of the Minors and Nits, and committed the item.

**Decisions made without anyone to ask.** All are recorded in `docs/progress/v1.4/work/F2/build.md`:
- **Plate length:** it stays up 2540 ms, not the decided 1800 ms (`NOTE_MIN_MS`), so it is whole for as long as any named turn. This departure is written into 13 §6 and the `CREW_FOLD_MS` row in 15.
- **The 300 ms tell is kept:** the reviewer read "the phases shrink to the flight plus the arrival" as leaving the length at 2815 ms. That reading is unconfirmed.
- **An existing e2e test was relaxed:** solar-dense "a captain's turn: named once parked" requires a ship to be parked while its name shows. That contradicts the decided plate that moves with the ship, so the test now skips summons whose plate is moving and checks the rest as before. This is the one place an existing test got weaker, so please check it.

**Side effects worth knowing:**
- **Quasar:** its directed run gets about 2.1 s longer because the pacing director picks a slower tempo.
- **Pulsar with every speed-up on:** first measured 3.9 s slower; after the fixes it is 0.2 s faster. The new `F2+` ledger row now records this.

Everything is recorded in `docs/progress/v1.4/work/F2/`: `tests.md`, `build.md` and `review.md`.
